gotchas: The vendor page opens Paddle as an overlay iframe named paddle_frame. A driver whose click cannot reach into a frame is stuck there: read that iframe's src and open it top level instead, swapping display_mode=overlay for display_mode=inline. Every field and button is then in the top frame.

Checkout is two steps, not one. Step one is email, country select and postcode; a Continue button gates step two. The card inputs do not exist in the DOM until Continue succeeds, so waiting on #cardNumber is the reliable signal that step one was accepted.

Card fields are plain top-frame inputs (#cardNumber, #cardHolder, #expiry, #cvv) despite js.stripe.com frames being present on the page — those frames are only the Google Pay and browser-wallet buttons, not the card surface. Do not go looking for a Stripe payment element here.
Expiry is a single combined field with an MM / YY placeholder; four digits typed straight in are accepted.

Paddle is merchant of record, so tax is added at step two only: the $29.00 list price becomes $31.57 at the pay button. Any spending-limit check should use the step-two total, not the advertised price.

Paddle runs its own invisible hCaptcha and a human-security frame on the payment step. Neither asked for interaction on this run, but they are the thing to look at first if a fill starts failing silently.
